title: THE ADVOCATES’ WELFARE FUND ACT, 2001
long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of a welfare fund for the benefit of advocates and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

sections.section_title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.text: (1) This Act may be called the Advocates’ Welfare Fund Act, 2001. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint; and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act and for different States. (Came into force on 1st November, 2001 for whole of India except certain States vide S.O. 946(E).)

sections.section_title: Definitions
sections.text: Defines key terms including: "advocate" (name entered in State roll under Advocates Act, 1961 and member of State Bar Association or State Advocates’ Association); "appropriate Government" (State Government or Central Government for Union territories); "cessation of practice"; "Chairperson"; "chartered accountant"; "dependants"; "Fund"; "insurer"; "member of the Fund"; "notification"; "prescribed"; "Schedule"; "scheduled bank"; "stamp"; "State"; "State Advocates’ Association"; "State Bar Association"; "State Bar Council"; "suspension of practice"; "Trustee Committee"; "Vakalatnama"; and provides that undefined terms take meanings from the Advocates Act, 1961.

sections.section_title: Advocates’ Welfare Fund
sections.text: (1) The appropriate Government shall constitute a fund to be called the "Advocates’ Welfare Fund". (2) There shall be credited to the Fund: (a) amounts paid by a State Bar Council under section 15; (b) any other contribution by a State Bar Council; (c) voluntary donations or contributions by Bar Council of India, State Bar Associations, State Advocates’ Associations, institutions, advocates or other persons; (d) grants by Central or State Government; (e) sums borrowed under section 12; (f) sums collected under section 18; (g) sums received from LIC or other insurers on death of members under Group Insurance; (h) profits, dividends or refunds from such policies; (i) interest, dividend or return on investments; (j) sums collected by sale of stamps under section 26. (3) Sums shall be paid to or collected by such agencies, at such intervals and in such manner as may be prescribed.

sections.section_title: Establishment of Trustee Committee
sections.text: (1) With effect from such date as the appropriate Government may by notification appoint, there shall be established a Trustee Committee called the "Advocates’ Welfare Fund Trustee Committee". (2) It shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and common seal, with power to acquire, hold and dispose of property, and may sue and be sued in its name. (3) Composition: (a) Advocate-General of the State as Chairperson, ex officio (or a senior advocate nominated by appropriate Government where there is no Advocate-General); (b) Secretary, Law Department – Member, ex officio; (c) Secretary, Home Department – Member, ex officio; (d) Chairman of State Bar Council – Member, ex officio; (e) Government Pleader or Public Prosecutor nominated by appropriate Government – Member; (f) two advocates nominated by State Bar Council – Members; (g) Secretary of State Bar Council – Secretary, ex officio. (4)-(5) Nominated Chairperson and Members hold office for a period not exceeding three years.

sections.section_title: Disqualifications and removal of Chairperson or Member of Trustee Committee
sections.text: (1) The appropriate Government shall remove the Chairperson or any Member who: (a) is or has been adjudged insolvent; (b) has become physically or mentally incapable; (c) has been convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude; (d) has acquired financial or other interest likely to affect functions prejudicially; (e) has abused position so as to render continuation detrimental to public interest; or (f) is absent without leave for more than three consecutive meetings (subject to condonation). (2) No removal under (d) or (e) without reasonable opportunity of being heard.

sections.section_title: Resignation by nominated Chairperson and Members of Trustee Committee and filling up of casual vacancy
sections.text: (1) Nominated Chairperson or Member under clause (e) may resign by three months’ notice to the appropriate Government. (2) Member under clause (f) may resign by three months’ notice to the State Bar Council. (3)-(4) Casual vacancies shall be filled as soon as may be; the person nominated holds office only for the residual term of the original incumbent.

sections.section_title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of Trustee Committee
sections.text: No act or proceeding of the Trustee Committee shall be invalid merely by reason of any vacancy or defect in constitution, any defect or irregularity in nomination, or any irregularity in procedure not affecting the merits of the case.

sections.section_title: Meetings of Trustee Committee
sections.text: (1) The Trustee Committee shall meet at least once in every three calendar months and at least four times every year. (2) Three Members form the quorum. (3) Chairperson (or any other Member chosen by those present) shall preside. (4) Questions decided by majority vote; Chairperson or presiding Member has a second or casting vote in case of equality.

sections.section_title: Travelling and daily allowances to nominated Chairperson and Members of Trustee Committee
sections.text: The nominated Chairperson and Members under clauses (e) and (f) of section 4(3) shall be entitled to travelling and daily allowances as are admissible to members of the State Bar Council.

sections.section_title: Vesting and application of Fund
sections.text: The Fund shall vest in, and be held and applied by, the Trustee Committee subject to the provisions, and for the purposes, of this Act.

sections.section_title: Functions of Trustee Committee
sections.text: (1) Subject to this Act and any other law, the Trustee Committee shall administer the Fund. (2) Without prejudice to generality, it shall: (a) hold amounts and assets in trust; (b) receive and dispose of applications for admission or re-admission within ninety days; (c) receive applications for payment, conduct enquiry and dispose within five months; (d) record decisions in minutes book; (e) pay amounts at rates specified in Schedule I; (f) send periodical and annual reports to appropriate Government and State Bar Council; (g) communicate decisions by registered post or electronic mode; (h) do such other acts as required under this Act and rules.

sections.section_title: Borrowing and investment
sections.text: (1) The Trustee Committee may, with prior approval of the appropriate Government and State Bar Council, borrow any sum required for the purposes of this Act. (2) It shall deposit monies in any scheduled bank or invest in debt instruments of corporations owned/controlled by the appropriate Government, loans floated by it, or in any other manner directed by the State Bar Council with prior approval. (3) All amounts due and payable and all expenditure relating to management and administration shall be paid out of the Fund.

sections.section_title: Accounts and audit
sections.text: (1) The Trustee Committee shall maintain proper accounts and prepare annual statement of accounts and annual report in such form and manner as may be prescribed. (2) Accounts shall be audited annually by a chartered accountant appointed by the State Bar Council. (3) Audited accounts and report shall be forwarded to the State Bar Council, which may issue directions. (4) The Trustee Committee shall comply with such directions. (5) Audit charges shall be paid from the Fund as fixed by the State Bar Council.

sections.section_title: Powers and duties of Secretary
sections.text: The Secretary shall: (a) be the chief executive authority and responsible for carrying out decisions; (b) represent the Committee in suits and proceedings; (c) authenticate decisions and instruments by signature; (d) operate bank account jointly with the Chairperson; (e) convene meetings and prepare minutes; (f) attend meetings with necessary records; (g) maintain forms, registers and records and do correspondence; (h) prepare annual statement of business; (i) do such other acts as directed by the Trustee Committee and State Bar Council.

sections.section_title: Payment of certain monies to Fund by State Bar Council
sections.text: The State Bar Council shall pay to the Fund annually an amount equal to twenty per cent. of the enrolment fee received by it under clause (f) of section 24 of the Advocates Act, 1961.

chapters.chapter_title: RECOGNITION OF ANY ASSOCIATION OF ADVOCATES

sections.section_title: Recognition by a State Bar Council of any association of advocates
sections.text: (1) Any association of advocates registered before commencement of this Act may, before a date notified by the State Bar Council, apply for recognition in the prescribed form. (2) Any association registered on or after commencement may apply within three months of registration. (3) Application shall be accompanied by copy of rules/bye-laws, names and addresses of office bearers, and list of members with particulars. (4) State Bar Council may, after enquiry, recognise the association and issue certificate of recognition. (5) Decision of State Bar Council on recognition shall be final. Explanation: "registered" means registered or deemed registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 or any other law for the time being in force.

sections.section_title: Duties of State Bar Associations and State Advocates’ Associations
sections.text: (1) Every State Bar Association and State Advocates’ Association shall, on or before the 15th day of April every year, furnish to the State Bar Council a list of its members as on 31st March of that year. (2) They shall inform the State Bar Council of: (a) any change in membership including admissions and re-admissions within thirty days; (b) death or other cessation of practice or voluntary suspension of practice of any member within thirty days of occurrence; (c) such other matters as may be required by the State Bar Council from time to time.

chapters.chapter_title: MEMBERSHIP AND PAYMENT OUT OF ADVOCATES’ WELFARE FUND

sections.section_title: Membership in Fund
sections.text: (1) Every advocate practising before commencement of this Act in any court, tribunal or other authority in a State and being a member of a State Bar Association or State Advocates’ Association shall apply, within six months of commencement, to the Trustee Committee for admission as a member of the Fund in the prescribed form. (2) Every person admitted as an advocate on the roll of a State Bar Council after commencement, and practising in any court etc. and being a member of a State Bar Association or State Advocates’ Association, shall apply within six months of enrolment for admission as a member of the Fund.

sections.section_title: Ex gratia grant to a member of Fund
sections.text: The Trustee Committee may, on an application made by a member of the Fund, or his nominee or legal heir, grant an ex gratia amount from the Fund in cases of permanent disability or other prescribed circumstances, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed.

sections.section_title: Review
sections.text: The Trustee Committee may, of its own motion or on application, review any order passed by it and pass such order as it thinks fit.

sections.section_title: Payment of amount on cessation of practice
sections.text: On cessation of practice, a member of the Fund or his nominee or legal heir shall be entitled to receive from the Fund an amount at the rate specified in Schedule I, calculated with reference to the period of practice as a member of the Fund.

sections.section_title: Restriction on alienation, attachment, etc., of interest of member in Fund
sections.text: The interest of a member of the Fund in the Fund or any amount payable out of the Fund shall not be assigned, transferred, pledged, charged, attached or made the subject of any other form of security, and shall not pass to any receiver, assignee or official liquidator.

sections.section_title: Exemption from income-tax
sections.text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Income-tax Act, 1961, any amount paid under this Act shall be exempt from income-tax.

sections.section_title: Group Life Insurance for members of Fund and other benefits
sections.text: The Trustee Committee may obtain Group Life Insurance policies for members of the Fund and provide such other benefits as it may consider appropriate, subject to the availability of funds and such conditions as may be prescribed.

sections.section_title: Appeal against decision or order of Trustee Committee
sections.text: Any person aggrieved by a decision or order of the Trustee Committee may prefer an appeal to the appropriate Government within such time and in such manner as may be prescribed; the decision of the appropriate Government on such appeal shall be final.

chapters.chapter_title: PRINTING, DISTRIBUTION AND CANCELLATION OF STAMPS

sections.section_title: Printing and distribution of Advocates’ Welfare Fund Stamps by State Bar Council
sections.text: The State Bar Council shall cause to be printed and distributed Advocates’ Welfare Fund Stamps of such design, denomination and colour as may be prescribed, and shall supply them to the associations recognised under section 16 for sale to advocates.

sections.section_title: Vakalatnama to bear stamps
sections.text: Every advocate shall affix on every Vakalatnama filed by him stamps of the value specified in Schedule II, and no Vakalatnama shall be accepted by any court, tribunal or other authority unless it bears the required stamps; the value of stamps shall be in addition to the court-fee payable.

sections.section_title: Certain persons not to be eligible for benefits
sections.text: No person who is in receipt of any pension or other benefit from the Central Government, a State Government or any local authority by reason of having held any office under such Government or authority shall be eligible for any benefit under this Act.

sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
sections.text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the appropriate Government, the Trustee Committee, the State Bar Council or any of their officers or employees for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act or any rule made thereunder.

sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
sections.text: No civil court shall have jurisdiction to settle, decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act required to be settled, decided or dealt with or to be determined by the Trustee Committee or the appropriate Government.

sections.section_title: Power to summon witnesses and take evidence
sections.text: The Trustee Committee shall have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 while trying a suit in respect of summoning and enforcing attendance of witnesses, requiring production of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavits.

sections.section_title: Power to amend Schedules I and II
sections.text: The appropriate Government may, by notification, amend Schedule I or Schedule II, and every such notification shall be laid before the State Legislature or Parliament, as the case may be.

sections.section_title: Power of appropriate Government to issue directions
sections.text: The appropriate Government may, from time to time, issue to the Trustee Committee such directions as it may consider necessary for the efficient administration of the Fund, and the Trustee Committee shall comply with such directions.

sections.section_title: Power of appropriate Government to supersede Trustee Committee
sections.text: If the appropriate Government is of opinion that the Trustee Committee is unable to perform, or has persistently made default in the performance of, the duties imposed on it by or under this Act, or has exceeded or abused its powers, it may, by notification, supersede the Trustee Committee for such period as may be specified, and make such arrangements for the administration of the Fund during the period of supersession as it may think fit.

sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
sections.text: The Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act in relation to Union territories and in respect of such other matters as may be prescribed.

sections.section_title: Power of State Government to make rules
sections.text: The State Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act in relation to the State, including the form of applications, the manner of payment of contributions, the procedure for meetings of the Trustee Committee, and other matters required to be prescribed.

sections.section_title: Rules and notifications to be laid before Parliament or State Legislature
sections.text: Every rule made by the Central Government and every notification issued under section 32 by the Central Government shall be laid before each House of Parliament; every rule made by a State Government and every notification issued under section 32 by a State Government shall be laid before the State Legislature, in the manner provided for the laying of rules under the respective legislative procedure.

sections.section_title: Saving
sections.text: Nothing in this Act shall affect any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under any other law for the time being in force, or any legal proceeding or remedy in respect of any such right, privilege, obligation or liability.

schedules.title: SCHEDULE I
schedules.description: Rates of amount payable on cessation of practice (as specified in the Act; actual rates may be amended by notification under section 32).

schedules.title: SCHEDULE II
schedules.description: Value of Advocates’ Welfare Fund Stamps to be affixed on Vakalatnama (as specified in the Act; actual values may be amended by notification under section 32).
